newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand projects 1997 c/a deficit will narrow.
newsitem.headline: Thailand projects 1997 c/a deficit will narrow.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand (BOT) projected on Thursday that the country's 1997 current account deficit would narrow to 7.1 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from 8.2 percent seen in 1996 and 8.1 percent in 1995.

The central bank said, when releasing its projections for key economic indicators in 1996 and 1996, that the country's trade deficit would also widen to 474 billion baht next year from 434 billion baht seen in 1996.
The central bank said exports in 1997 were projected at 1.486 trillion baht against imports of 1.960 trillion baht and that would leave a trade deficit of 474 billion baht.
A trade deficit of 434 billion baht was seen for this year on projected exports of 1.380 trillion baht against imports of 1.814 trillion baht, it added.
The BOT also projected Thailand's GDP would expand by 7.1 percent next year against 6.7 growth estimated for 1996 and 8.7 percent achieved in 1995.
Thai exports were seen growing by 7.7 percent over a 0.1 percent contraction seen in 1996 and robust 23.6 percent growth posted for 1995, the central bank added.
Inflation growth for 1997 was projected to average 4.8 percent against 5.8 percent expected in 1996 and 5.8 percent recorded in 1995.
